title: Why twelve columns look different
position: Central east–west nave of the Great Hypostyle Hall.
observation: Twelve columns have taller shafts and capitals shaped like open papyrus blooms, unlike the 122 shorter closed-bud papyrus columns in the side wings.
interpretation: The taller colonnade carried the elevated roof over the central aisle, enabling clerestory light to enter above the side roofs.
lookFor: Roof and clerestory remains above the central aisle.
uncertainties: Current visitor sightlines and lighting require field validation.
